correctness.rationale: For a binary order-n de Bruijn cycle, the feedback permutation has 2^(n-1) entries with two fixed endpoint bits. Cross-joining two full cycles exchanges successors in two conjugate-state pairs and toggles exactly two interior feedback bits. Relative to any clique vertex, the pairs toggled to all other vertices form a pairwise-intersecting family of 2-subsets of q=2^(n-1)-2 coordinates. Such a family is either a star (size <=q-1) or a triangle of at most three edges; hence omega<=q for every n>=4. For n=5, independently enumerated all 2^16=65536 feedback masks by their exact 32-state successor orbits, obtaining 2048 full cycles. Every 14-clique must be a rooted star: 224 valid (mask,common-coordinate) witnesses were enumerated, and each clique is counted exactly fourteen times, so exactly 16 distinct K14. At n=4, 16 valid masks and 24 rooted witnesses give 4 K6. A separate 6-mer-factor intersection check verified all pairs in the 16 constructed order-5 cliques. Finite exhaustive n=4,5 enumeration verifies only those orders; the universal n>=4 bound follows from the 2-subset lemma.

value.rationale: The graph of cross-joins is a natural object for nonlinear-feedback sequence generation. Its general clique bound and complete small-order extremal classification supply exact simultaneous cross-join structure not recovered from connectivity, degrees, or pairwise perturbation counts. The order-five census covers all 2048 cycles and is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary sample.

limitations: The universal bound depends on the exact cross-join/two-toggling equivalence reconstructed from the feedback mechanism.
Exact counts apply only to n=4,5 and count literal labelled cycle-subsets, not symmetry classes.
